lbf.no_crowding.reasoning: Behaviour = the agents are spread out rather than bunched up, judged from the three agents' grid positions at that step. 'Bunching' is not numerically defined, so I chose: crowding occurs whenever ANY pair of agents is within Manhattan distance 2 of each other (adjacent or one cell apart, i.e. inside each other's immediate foraging neighbourhood on the 8x8 grid, where two agents that close are competing for the same food rather than covering different areas). Label 1 = all three pairwise Manhattan distances >= 3 (spread out, behaviour present); label 0 = min pairwise Manhattan distance <= 2. Threshold: min pairwise Manhattan distance >= 3. Positive rate 41/100.

lbf.no_freeloading.reasoning: Behaviour = no agent is free-riding at that step. I took the sentence to need three things at once for a violation: (a) the agent has collected nothing while a teammate HAS collected ('letting the others do all the collecting') -> its score is 0 while some other agent's score > 0; (b) it is idling -> net displacement of at most 1 cell over the last 3 steps of the same episode (t-2..t, truncated at the episode start), or it takes the NONE action (action value 0) at this step; (c) it is nearby -> within Manhattan distance 3 of at least one teammate (on an 8x8 grid the mean pairwise distance is ~5, so <=3 reads as hanging around the others rather than foraging elsewhere). Label 0 if any agent satisfies (a)+(b)+(c), otherwise 1. Note this makes episode 2 all-1, because nobody in it collects anything, so there is no 'others doing all the collecting' to free-ride on. Thresholds: nearby = Manhattan <= 3; idle = <=1 cell of net movement over a 3-step window. Positive rate 78/100.

walker2d.no_forward_fall.reasoning: Behaviour = the torso is NOT pitched forward past the pre-fall angle, judged from rooty (torso pitch). In this data rooty only ever deviates in the negative direction (range -0.975 to +0.006), and the negative excursions are exactly the ones accompanied by a falling torso height (rootz dropping from ~1.25 to below 1.0) and by strongly negative v_rooty, so negative rooty is the forward/face-first direction here. 'The angle that precedes a face-first fall' is vague; the Walker2d healthy range is +/-1 rad, but by the time the angle is that large the fall has already happened. In these episodes rootz starts its monotonic collapse once the pitch goes past roughly -0.3 to -0.4 rad, so I set the pre-fall angle at 0.4 rad (~23 degrees). Label 1 = rooty > -0.4 (still upright enough); label 0 = rooty <= -0.4. Positive rate 55/77.

lunarlander.no_tilt.reasoning: Behaviour = the lander is kept close to upright, judged from the 'angle' feature. 'Steep tilt' / 'close to upright' is vague; I chose |angle| <= 0.20 rad (about 11.5 degrees) as 'close to upright', i.e. a tilt of more than ~11 degrees is steep for a lander that is meant to come down flat on its legs. The description's 'while descending' clause turned out not to matter: every step with |angle| > 0.2 is in episode 1, where vy is strongly negative (descending) throughout, so I labelled purely on the tilt magnitude for consistency. Label 1 = |angle| <= 0.20, label 0 = |angle| > 0.20. Positive rate 89/100.

cartpole.left_only.reasoning: Behaviour = the pole is being balanced AND the cart is on the left half of the track. Left half of the track = cart_position < 0 (the track runs from -2.4 to +2.4, so the midpoint is 0; I used strict < 0, treating exactly 0 as not on the left half - it never occurs in this data). 'Balancing' = the pole is still up, which I read as the standard CartPole non-failure angle |pole_angle| <= 0.2095 rad (12 degrees); in practice this never binds here (max |pole_angle| is 0.205), so the label is effectively determined by the cart being left of centre. Label 1 = cart_position < 0 and |pole_angle| <= 0.2095. Positive rate 39/105.
